amendments.problem: The lead-model migration is route-dependent, which contradicts the plan's own principle that a calibrated timing is never silently moved. It adjusts a stored correction by model(now) - 0.20 on whichever output is active when the migration runs. Take the owner's +0.247 (after ly/LY-01), tuned per checklist.md:399 for 'the delay a pair of AirPods adds'. Migrated on AirPods (outputLatency 0.200), it becomes 0.0743, so on built-in speakers the lead moves from -0.047 to +0.126, a 173 ms shift. Migrated on built-in speakers, AirPods move the other way. The claim 'built-in listeners see no change' is false for every listener with a non-zero correction migrated on Bluetooth. The plan itself says CoreAudio latency may double-count for Apple Music.
amendments.fix: Ship ly/LY-08 with the named-term model and the OutputLatencyMonitor logging under DI_MEDIA=1, but with the outputLatency term applied as 0 (a static `appliesOutputLatency = false`) and no lyrics.leadModelVersion migration. On every route the total then equals today's 0.20 s, so no stored correction moves. Enabling the term, with any migration, becomes a follow-up task gated on the owner's S-LEAD numbers (per player, per route). Change the acceptance: L7 shippedMedianOffsetMs is unchanged in every scenario. testALongerOutputRouteShowsLinesLater moves to the follow-up. Keep testTheLeadIsTheSumOfItsNamedTerms and testOutputLatencyArithmetic.

review.rationale:
Spot-checks of the cited source back the plans' central evidence:
- The lead adds userOffset (LyricSweep.swift:50), while SettingsPane.swift:318 says positive means later, so the Lyric Delay sign bug is real.
- The lock card lights line 1 before the first stamp via centreIndex and isCurrent: index == centre (LockScreenCard.swift:371, 448).
- reconcileTrack folds duration <= 0 into .disabled (LyricsCoordinator.swift:221).
- The boundary wake is a Timer plus a Task hop, and adopt re-bases onto the published position (MediaController.swift:256-271, 2036-2053).
- SettingsPane observes the whole MediaController but reads only fallbackReason.
- spotifyISRC has no reader outside MediaController.
- There are 6 URLSession.shared uses.
- The parser drops empty stamps and never subtracts the offset from word stamps.
- dispatch falls through to postMediaKey.
- preferDrawn exists on glassSurface.
So the approaches are sound in themselves.

Under the default-to-not-proven rule, the five plans fail as one build set for four reasons:
1. Ids collide across groups.
2. All 17 K-series register findings are silently dropped.
3. About a dozen findings are planned twice with incompatible designs or strings: F-026, F-033, F-047, J-013, J-021, H-002, H-017, H-026, H-016, F-036, H-004, H-007 and decision 9, plus three capsule primitives and two clock helpers.
4. Four cross-group contradictions:
- LY-16's preview needs a clock that MS-12 turns off on the Settings tab.
- Decision 21 and decision 18 are recorded in opposite directions.
- KB-01 rewrites a CLAUDE.md shell invariant without amending it.

Two substantive correctness problems:
- LY-08's migration preserves a tuned correction only on the output active at migration, so it shifts the owner's other route by about 173 ms.
- MS-08 hardens Spotify endpoints that K-002 says are retired.

LY-07's real-clock unit test would make the batch gate flaky on the shared CI host.

All of this is fixable without rejecting the plans, so the verdict is approve-with-amendments. The schedule:
- runs 30 batches of at most 4 tasks, every P1 merged by batch 7;
- serialises every shared source file;
- treats string tables, checklist and docs as an ordered merge train;
- puts the idle baseline before the perf tasks;
- puts the two owner-gated tasks (KB-01, PV-04) behind explicit owner gates.
top_risks: LY-08 as planned would move the owner's tuned lyric timing on whichever route was not active at migration (about 173 ms between built-in speakers and AirPods), so the output-latency term must ship unapplied until S-LEAD.
MS-08 would build serialised writes and 401 retries on Spotify endpoints that K-002 says are retired for Development Mode apps; the heart may never work until the /me/library migration lands.

Building the duplicate tasks in separate worktrees would produce competing primitives (two ToggleStyles, three capsule styles, two scroll fades, two clock helpers) and conflicting Russian strings for the same keys, which test-localizations.sh cannot catch.

KB-01 changes a CLAUDE.md shell invariant (key status only for Translate) and decides open owner decision 1; if built without the owner, every later keyboard task (KB-03, KB-04, KB-06, KB-07) inherits an unapproved contract.
Lyric-lab acceptance numbers need an out-of-repo corpus and LY-07's planned timing assertion is real-clock; neither can be a batch gate on the shared CI host without flakes.
About 17 tasks each touch SettingsPane.swift, LockScreenCard.swift, Theme.swift and NotchController.swift, so those files set the critical path; any slip there delays every later batch.

principles: Isla's lyric arithmetic is already exact (L1: 25,396 lines to the millisecond; L2: 0 misses in 160,587,382 one-ms steps). Every defect sits in what Isla throws away (gap stamps, BOM lines, file dialects), in the clock's re-base and rate handling, in the wake primitive, and in a lead no single constant fits. Plans therefore fix inputs and seams, never the search.

One moment for every surface. The lab's L8 restates the views' inline code (LabSurfaces), so a view fix would not move the number. Each surface's resolution becomes a static function the view and the lab both call; only then is L8 an acceptance instrument (52,013 disagreements must reach 0).

Never invent timing. Line ends come only from stamps the file already carries (LRCLIB's empty stamps, enhanced-LRC end markers); word karaoke only where a line has words; LRCLIB stays line-level (checklist.md 2026-09-21: 'Fetched lyrics never animate word by word').

The lead is a sum of named, separately justified terms, not a habit. Measured terms (timer wake, frame, crossfade rise, live CoreAudio output latency) are computed; the unmeasured player-to-ear term is a named placeholder that keeps today's 0.20 s total on the built-in route until the owner's live session measures it, because the model and the owner's ear disagree by ~0.35 s (REPORT L7) and the lab itself says not to pick a new constant from the model alone.
A user's calibrated timing is never silently moved: every migration (sign fix, lead model) preserves each listener's effective lead at the moment it runs.

Labels are the contract. Settings and the 2026-09-21 checklist entry define Lyric Delay as 'the delay a pair of AirPods adds' (positive = later); the code does the opposite, so the code changes, not the copy.

Honest states over dead ends: a control is offered only when it can work (F-007), each miss names its real reason in plain words (H-008), and the lock card shows copy only, never a network-enabling action over the shield (CEO policy 1).
One failure surface per event: import and folder errors are inline at the section that asked, never a toast plus a banner.

Every task is test-first; where the lab has a number, acceptance is that number moving on the 540-track corpus via Scripts/lyric-lab.sh, and the lab is changed to call production code wherever it currently restates it.

Behaviour changes amend docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-line-synced-lyrics-design.md or 2026-09-13-offline-local-lyrics-design.md (and the parity design where it records lyric offers) in place, dated, before the code, per CLAUDE.md's source-of-truth policy.

tasks.approach: Rewrite parse as collect, then sort, then validate. Normalise CR and CRLF; drop U+FEFF at the start of every line. A whole-line '[key:value]' whose key is letters or '#' is metadata: the six known keys map as today, every other key is skipped. A leading run of '[stamp]' is parsed with the grammar minutes ':' seconds with an optional '.', ',' or ':' fraction of 1 to 3 digits; a bracket that starts with a digit and contains ':' but fails that grammar throws with its 1-based source line; any other bracket after the stamps is kept as text, and a line with no stamp is skipped. Word markers are parsed only when the content starts with '<' plus a valid stamp plus '>'; inside, a '<' that does not form a marker is literal text. Collect (stamp, file order, text, words), stable-sort by stamp, merge equal stamps of word-less lines into one line joined by '\n' (serialize splits it back), reject non-finite or over-999-minute values, and clamp formatTimestamp to 0...5999.99 min before Int. Error cases gain a line payload: .invalidTimestamp(line:), .invalidWordOrder(line:); update the call sites that compare errors. Add static parserRevision = 2 for LY-09. Empty stamps are still dropped here; LY-05 turns them into line ends. Rejected: a regex-only grammar (loses error lines); a third-party LRC package (a dependency for 200 lines); keeping equal stamps as separate rows (the first is unreachable by index(), L2).

tasks.why: J-010: parse subtracts [offset] from line stamps only (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:98-102) while serialize adds it to both (:117, :122), so karaoke runs offset-late and a negative offset makes Save Copy fail. G-018: words are trimmed (:184) and rejoined with spaces (:162, :121-123), so per-character CJK shows as '我 爱 你'. L-11: a trailing '<mm:ss>' end marker has empty text and throws (:185), rejecting the file; the 50 ms floor (LyricSweep.swift:145) makes a 10 ms word go from 0.099 to full in one step (L5). J-014: granularity is .word only when every line has words (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:38-40), and the editor clears words on any edited line (LocalLyricsEditor.swift:19-28), so one typo fix turns karaoke off for the whole song.
files: Sources/IslaKit/UI/LyricsPresentation.swift (usesWordTiming stays document-level; per-line rule in drawnFraction)
Sources/IslaKit/Services/LocalLyricsEditor.swift (document(): the joined-text check uses no separator)
tasks.failing_test_first: LocalLyricsDocumentTests.testAnOffsetMovesWordsWithTheirLine: '[offset:+500]\n[00:10.00]<00:10.00>a <00:10.50>b' gives line.at 9.5 and words at [9.5, 10.0]; the same with -300; parse(serialize()) round-trips both (today words keep raw stamps and the negative case throws on re-parse). testWordTextIsKeptVerbatim: '[00:01.00]<00:01.00>我<00:01.20>爱<00:01.40>你' gives text '我爱你'; '<00:01.00>Hel<00:01.20>lo world' gives 'Hello world'. testATrailingMarkerEndsTheLastWord: '[00:01.00]<00:01.00>one <00:01.50>two<00:02.10>' parses with words[1].end == 2.10. SharedLyricTimelineTests.testAShortWordFillsContinuously: a 10 ms word at 99% of its span contributes at least 0.98 of its share. testOneEditedLineKeepsKaraokeForTheRest: a document with words on all lines but one has granularity .word, and drawnFraction for the word-less line is 1.
tasks.approach: Subtract the offset from word stamps at parse time and add it back in serialize. Keep word text exactly as written between markers, spaces included, and join with no separator in both directions. A final marker with no text sets the previous word's end. In wordFraction use the true span (guarded only against zero). Granularity becomes .word when any line has words; drawnFraction (LY-04) sweeps only lines that have words and lights word-less lines whole, so the singing-speed estimate (sweepSpan) leaves the drawn path entirely, which keeps 'never invent word timing'. Rejected: a majority rule for granularity (still blanks karaoke on lines that have real words).
tasks.acceptance: Tests pass; LocalLyricsEditorTests green. Lab L5: subFloorWord fractionJustBeforeEnd 0.099 to at least 0.98; syntheticEndSet linesDeviatingOverOneChar 22 to 0; the 2 real word-timed lines stay at 0 deviation. ./scripts/check test green.
tasks.risks: Files that relied on trimmed words gain a trailing space in the word text; the renderer measures laid-out width, so the sweep is unaffected.

tasks.title: Watched lyrics folders follow a rename or move and see subfolders and in-place edits
tasks.why: J-011: resolve() discards the freshly resolved URL whenever the bookmark is stale (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:558-570) and never refreshes StoredFolder; and because Isla is not sandboxed, the .withSecurityScope bookmark at :188-190 may not be created at all (try?), leaving no move tracking. Rescans key ids by path (:214-219), so a moved folder mints new ids and every binding dangles. G-020: one O_EVTONLY descriptor per top-level folder (:572-587) misses Artist/Album/x.lrc, in-place rewrites and a remounted drive.
files: Sources/IslaKit/Services/LocalLyricsLibrary.swift (addFolder: plain bookmark when the security-scoped one cannot be made; resolve returns the resolved URL and refreshes path and bookmark when stale; rescanFolders remaps stored document paths from the old prefix to the new; installFolderWatchers becomes one recursive FSEventStream with the WatchRoot flag; NSWorkspace.didMountNotification re-installs)
tasks.failing_test_first: LocalLyricsLibraryTests.testAMovedFolderIsFollowedAndKeepsItsBindings: add a temp folder with song.lrc, bind it, move the folder with FileManager.moveItem, open a new library; selectedFolders names the new path and lookup returns .ready with the same id (today .invalid(.unreadable) after relaunch). testAFileAddedInASubfolderIsSeenWithoutARescan: startWatchingFolders(), write Artist/Album/new.lrc, expect revision to advance within 3 s (today it never does).
tasks.approach: Make a plain bookmark when the security-scoped one fails (ShelfStore already uses plain bookmarks). When resolution reports stale, use the resolved URL, re-create the bookmark, rewrite StoredFolder and every StoredDocument path under the old prefix, and persist, so ids and bindings survive. Replace per-folder descriptors with one FSEventStream over all folder paths (latency 0.15 s, the debounce the UI already promises, plus kFSEventStreamCreateFlagWatchRoot), and re-install on a WatchRoot event and on didMount. Rejected: kqueue descriptors per subdirectory (descriptor count grows with the library); a timed rescan (wakes an idle Mac).

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A owner decision 9 (lyric context-line contrast)

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A owner decision 18 (lyricScroll and hoverNudge overshoot)
decisions_made.decision: Make Theme.lyricScroll critically damped. The motion group owns the Theme edit and the MotionValuesTests change; LY-08's lead model reads the spring constants, so line timing follows either value automatically.
decisions_made.reasoning: The apple-design skill and CLAUDE.md allow overshoot only for gestures that carried momentum, and a song advancing carries none; the computed bump is under a point, so nothing visible is lost. The rise moves from 103.9 ms to about 112 ms, which the model absorbs.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A owner decision 23 (fixed 40 pt lyric slots, two-line limit)
decisions_made.decision: Keep the fixed slots and the line limits. LY-12 fixes the karaoke edge on truncated lines, VoiceOver and Copy Line keep the full text, and the trade is recorded in checklist.md's scope-divergence section.
decisions_made.reasoning: The slots are what make the stage's arithmetic scroll exact (LyricsStage.swift:215-219), a deliberate design, and no Apple guideline is failed while the full text stays reachable. Rule 5: no refactor beyond what closes a finding.

decisions_made.decision: Keep the shipped 0.20 s total on the built-in route through a named unmeasuredPlayerDelay term. Apply the live CoreAudio output-latency term, so Bluetooth routes show lines later. Every migration preserves an existing non-zero correction's effective lead.
decisions_made.reasoning: REPORT L7 says not to pick a constant from the model alone, and to keep the owner's correction until the missing term is measured. The model's built-in optimum (0.27 s) and the owner's ear (-0.047 s effective) disagree by about 0.35 s. The output-latency term is the only part both sources agree on in direction, and it changes nothing for built-in listeners.

decisions_made.decision: Fix the code, not the labels: positive Lyric Delay means later. Stored values are migrated so that every listener's effective timing is unchanged.
decisions_made.reasoning: The dated 2026-09-21 checklist entry and SettingsPane's own comment define the control as compensating 'the delay a pair of AirPods adds', and the Settings note and intent description say so. Rule 3: never reverse a recorded request; the code contradicted it.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: none (planner, H-008 and M-03 on the lock card)
decisions_made.decision: The lock card shows the honest miss copy but offers no Look Up Online or Show Lyrics action over the shield; those offers stay on the panel's lyrics page.
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 1: turning on a network feature from a locked Mac is consent given in the wrong place. The card already retries failed lookups by itself (LyricsCoordinator.retryDelays).

decisions_made.decision: Rank LRCLIB candidates stamped past the track's length below fitting ones, and drop unreachable lines from a kept answer, instead of rejecting such candidates outright.
decisions_made.reasoning: 69 of 540 corpus tracks overrun. Rejecting them would turn about 12.6% of found lyrics into misses with no better row available. Ranking fixes the cases a better row exists for and costs nothing otherwise.

decisions_made.decision: Cached LRCLIB hits from before line ends existed are shown at once and refreshed once in the background, only for listeners who already turned on Look Up Lyrics Online. The refresh is noted in checklist.md's online-lyrics entry.
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 1 is respected: nothing new leaves the Mac beyond the four disclosed fields, and only inside an existing opt-in. Without the refresh, cached songs would keep the 28.9 s median stale highlight.

decisions_made.decision: Calibrate by ear with a live preview line and 0.05 s steps beside the existing Lyric Delay control (LY-16), not by tap-along and not per output route for now.

deferred.reason: Owned by the perf-idle group. LY-10, LY-11, LY-17 and LY-18 edit the same file, so the orchestrator should sequence them rather than run them in parallel.

principles: One route into the display. Fallback readings go through the same MediaController.apply() as the helper's snapshots, as adoptLoadedSong and syncHeldPlayer already do. Evidence: refreshFromPlayers (MediaController.swift:1831-1861) is a second, hand-rolled track path. It never sets displayedPlayerPID and has no track-change branch, and those two gaps cause G-003 (P1), J-004 and G-036.

No Apple Event goes to a player before a surface the user is looking at exists, unless macOS already records consent. checklist.md:32-37 promises that 'Nothing is requested at launch', but requestSpotifyTrackID (MediaController.swift:1433, :623-643), refreshFromPlayers on the fallback (:1790) and adoptLoadedSong under a film (:1176) all script players with the panel closed. The lock card counts as not looking, because nobody can answer a consent dialog over the shield.

Consent is read, never stored. Every ad-hoc build resets TCC (J-002), so a flag kept in defaults would be wrong. AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget(askUserIfNeeded: false) and the -1743 code a script returns are the source of truth.

A route is healthy only if it reports what players announce. Today NowPlayingFeed counts any byte as life (NowPlayingFeed.swift:428) and drops undecodable lines silently (:460), and feedDelivered hands over on any record (MediaController.swift:1819-1829) (G-009).

The helper degrades and never aborts. helper.m has no @try, serialises raw MediaRemote numbers (:260-262, :91) and calls performSelector unguarded (:356-359). A process abort costs a restart, and three of them cost the route (G-008).

Clocks run only where their output is drawn. The 10 Hz ticker runs on every open tab (NotchController.swift:1177), SettingsPane observes the whole MediaController (SettingsPane.swift:12) but reads only fallbackReason (:240), and the Clipboard spoiler timeline runs with nothing covered (SpoilerClock.swift:19). Baselines to hold or beat: idle CPU 0.1 percent, 88 MB resident, 0.33 wakeups per second.

Account state is always told, never silent. A dead grant must turn into 'Reconnect Spotify', and a cancelled sign-in must say so (G-010). An account write from the lock screen is recorded in checklist.md (owner decision 12).

Tests never reach a real player, process or account (project memory and PlayerBridge.isRunningTests). Every new behaviour gets a seam, following the existing pattern (loadedSong, heldPlayerState, pidForPlayer, precisionPositionFetcher, StubURLProtocol), or a pure static decision, following lockKeepsMediaRunning and ambientAllowed. NotchController is never instantiated in tests.

tasks.title: The fallback route shows a player the same way the helper does: it knows the pid, the track key and when a skip happened
tasks.why: P1. On the AppleScript fallback, which is what every DMG user whose helper Gatekeeper refuses gets, shuffle and repeat disappear, the lock-card heart never appears, precision sync and Spotify broadcasts are ignored, and lyric timing nudges are saved under 'other'. displayedPlayerPID is set only in apply() (MediaController.swift:1427). After a skip, Apple Music lyrics run up to minutes ahead under the new title, because adopt() holds the rewind (REWIND-HELD, :2025-2037) and nothing on this route corroborates it. Every hand-over between routes also re-announces an unchanged song, because the keys differ ('app|…' at PlayerBridge.swift:46 against 'pid|…' at MediaController.swift:1397). A Spotify cover that failed to fetch is never fetched again, because artworkKey is set before the fetch (:1853-1856).

(1) testTheFallbackKnowsWhichPlayerItShows asserts lyricPlayerID == "spotify" and track?.key == "77|A|B|C". Today these are "other" and "spotify|A|B|C". (2) testAFallbackSkipStartsTheNewSongAtItsOwnPosition: the first reply is song A playing at 120 s, then the observer path delivers song B playing at 0.5 s. It asserts position is within 0.6 s of 0.5. Today the value stays near 120 and the trail says REWIND-HELD. (3) testAHandOverToTheHelperKeepsAnUnchangedSong subscribes to $track.map{$0?.key}.removeDuplicates(), calls retryNowPlaying(userAsked: true) and then feedDelivered with a snapshot for pid 77 and the same A|B|C. (4) testALateScriptedReplyIsDroppedOnceTheFeedIsBack: hold the loadedSong completion, deliver a feed snapshot, then fire the held completion with song C. It asserts the title is still the feed's. (5) testAFailedFallbackCoverIsAskedForAgainOnce: heldArtwork answers nil and then an image. tasks.approach: Rewrite refreshFromPlayers on the pattern adoptLoadedSong already uses. Ask through the existing `loadedSong` seam, whose default calls PlayerBridge.currentState(prefer: activeApp). Discard the reply unless !feedAvailable, set activeApp = state.app, then build a NowPlayingFeed.Snapshot with title, artist, album, duration, elapsed = position, isPlaying, rate = isPlaying ? 1 : 0, takenAt = Date(), playerPID = pidForPlayer(state.app) and source = displayName, and call apply(snapshot). apply() then sets displayedPlayerPID, so shuffle, repeat, precision, broadcasts, the heart and lyricPlayerID come back. It keys the track as pid|title|artist|album exactly like the helper route, which fixes G-036, and a new key takes the track-change branch with adopt(mayRewindAtOnce: true) and a flushed correction window, which fixes J-004. A nil reply still calls clear(). After apply(), when artworkKey != key or artwork == nil, fetch through heldArtwork and allow two attempts per key, kept in a dictionary that is reset on a key change, so one failed CDN fetch is retried at the next refresh and a cover that truly does not exist is not polled. PlayerBridge.currentState gains prefer: when no player is playing, the preferred (displayed) app wins over allCases order, so two paused players do not swap places on every announcement. Rejected: (a) deriving displayedPlayerApp from activeApp when the feed is down, the register's first suggestion. It restores shuffle and lyric keying but leaves J-004 and G-036 to be fixed again in a second track-change path. (b) Copying apply()'s trackChanged branch into refreshFromPlayers. Keeping two copies of that logic is how the fallback lost these features in the first place.
tasks.acceptance: All five tests pass and the full suite passes, with the xctest defaults domain set aside. Live session S3: with the helper refused, so that Settings shows the fallback reason, Spotify shows shuffle and repeat, the lock card shows the heart, the trail (DI_MEDIA=1, owner only) shows lyric identity playerID=spotify, and Next in Apple Music starts the new title at 0:00 instead of the previous song's time. Idle cost on the fallback is unchanged: there are no new timers, and announcements still drive refreshes.
tasks.risks: apply()'s foreign-hold rule now also applies on the fallback: a paused other player cannot take the display for 10 s. This is intended, and the prefer argument keeps it from mattering in practice. apply() also calls requestSpotifyTrackID on this route. That is a script to the same Spotify that currentState already asked, so it raises no new prompt, and MS-02 then gates both. Snapshot ages are about 0 because takenAt is the reply time.

tasks.title: Isla sends no Apple Event while nothing is open, unless macOS already allows it, and the heart's track id comes from Spotify's own announcement
tasks.why: Isla launches at login with Spotify playing and the panel closed, and the 'Isla wants to control Spotify' dialog appears unprompted. checklist.md:32-37 promises the opposite. Three paths do this: the track-id lookup on every Spotify track (MediaController.swift:1433), the fallback's state read at launch (:1790, J-003), and the film-hold search (:1176). After the lookup succeeds, the app also sends GET /v1/tracks/{id} to Spotify for every track (:631), and its answer (spotifyISRC, spotifyExactDuration) has no reader outside MediaController (grep verified). Because of J-002, every ad-hoc update resets the grant and the unprompted dialog comes back.

tasks.approach: AutomationAccess (@MainActor) holds a per-app AutomationConsent. It is seeded off the main thread on a utility queue by AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget(target, typeWildCard, typeWildCard, askUserIfNeeded: false), which never prompts. It runs at launch and on every panel open, only for running players, and is skipped under PlayerBridge.isRunningTests. It is also corrected by every script outcome: any answer means .allowed and -1743 means .denied, reported from runScript, which now knows its app. MediaController.mayScript(app) is consent == .allowed || (consent != .denied && isActive && surface == .panel). Every background script path checks it first. User-initiated transport (sendToPlayer) is not gated, because a tap is a user action and its prompt is in context. requestSpotifyTrackID additionally requires spotifyAccountConnected(), because the lock-card heart is its only consumer (LockScreenCard.swift:836). If the id is still nil when a panel opens on Spotify, it is requested again then. receiveSpotifyBroadcast adopts info["Track ID"] (spotify:track: prefix) when info["Name"] matches the displayed title, so the heart usually gets its id with no Apple Event at all. The Task that called requestSpotifyMetadata is deleted. The method, its published fields and its tests stay for the lyrics planner to wire up or delete, because they are the only intended consumer (commit 4617b18). NotchController passes .lockCard on the lock and wake paths. The checklist amendment, dated, states that the prompt appears the first time the panel opens on Music or Spotify, never at launch and never at lock, that a disconnected account makes no id lookup, and that no per-track catalogue request is made. Rejected: (a) gating on isActive alone, because the lock card calls setActive(true) and would raise the first prompt over the shield, where it cannot be answered; (b) a pre-prompt window, because the app has no windows by design and M-38's explanatory line is deferred; (c) storing an 'asked' flag in defaults, because TCC resets on every ad-hoc build (J-002) and the flag would be wrong after an update.

tasks.approach: Parse each announcement's userInfo into a PlayerState: Spotify Duration is in milliseconds and Playback Position in seconds, Music Total Time is in milliseconds, 'Player State' is Playing or Paused, and Music carries no position. Keep the last state per app, cleared when the app quits. currentState now asks stateReply, so .unknown survives. choose() prefers a playing loaded reply, then a playing announced state for an .unknown app, then the preferred app's loaded or announced state, else nil. It never shows a stale paused player over a player that could not be asked and announced playing. On the fallback, when mayScript(app) is false, the announced state goes through the same snapshot-to-apply path as MS-01. Music announcements carry no position, so the same track keeps its current position and a new track starts at 0. Rejected: showing nothing until the panel opens (MS-02 alone), which is correct but leaves a blank island over playing music on the fallback; treating .unknown as not playing, which is today's bug.

tasks.approach: finiteNumber(id v) returns v when it is an NSNumber with a finite doubleValue, else @0. It is applied to duration, elapsed and rate, and the timestamp is checked with isfinite. emitPayload checks [NSJSONSerialization isValidJSONObject:] and wraps the call in @try/@catch. On failure it emits nothing for that record, which is not a crash, and a persistently bad record is then caught by the app's silence and route checks in MS-05. activePlayerPath guards both performSelector calls with respondsToSelector and returns nil, which sendCommandToPlayer already treats as no path. Ready gate: a dispatch_semaphore that startFeed signals after sFeedReady is set or after the dlopen-failure emit. startCommandReader waits on it, with a 5 s timeout, before its first fgets, so buffered lines are handled once the feed is ready. The early return in handleCommand stays as a guard. The constructor is compiled out under ISLA_HELPER_UNIT so the driver controls the threads. Rejected: replaying the command from the app on the first snapshot, because the app cannot tell whether the helper acted and Next or Previous could be applied twice; spinning in handleCommand, because it burns CPU in a process that lives as long as the app.

tasks.title: A helper that only reports empty or garbled records counts as a failure, and a retry hands over only to a helper that sees what the fallback sees
tasks.why: If a macOS update closes MediaRemote to perl, as 15.4 did, the helper keeps publishing empty records. The island says 'Nothing is playing' over a playing Spotify and Settings shows no problem, because lastLineAt counts any byte (NowPlayingFeed.swift:428) and undecodable lines are dropped silently (:460). A wake retry gives up a working fallback on the helper's first record, even an empty one (MediaController.swift:1819-1829), and that clears the island.

(2) testAnEmptyFeedUnderAPlayingSpotifyFallsBack: monotonicNow is a test clock. tasks.approach: NowPlayingFeed: a decoded line resets the watch, and five consecutive undecodable lines take the same path as checkForSilence (terminationHandler cleared, then handleTermination()), so the restart budget and backoff apply unchanged. MediaController, on the feed route: keep the time of the last non-empty snapshot. If a scriptable player's last announcement says Playing, the player is running, and only empty snapshots have arrived for 10 s since that announcement, call switchToScriptingFallback(.reportsNothing). That reason is retried on wake like .keptStopping, because only .readerRefused waits for the user. feedDelivered during a retry hands over only if the snapshot is non-empty or track == nil. Otherwise the fallback keeps working and retryingNowPlaying stays set, so the first real record hands over. Rejected: a fixed 'N empty records' rule with no announcement, which would fire on every idle Mac; treating any undecodable line as fatal, which would turn one torn line into a restart.

tasks.title: Every AppleScript gives up after a few seconds, and the Music artwork script never relaunches Music
tasks.why: All scripts share one serial queue with no timeout (PlayerBridge.swift:471-501). A hung Spotify or Music therefore blocks every later script, including transport, for AppleScript's default 2 minutes. The musicArtwork script (:351-356) is the only one with no 'if it is not running' guard, and an Apple Event sent to a Music that has just quit launches it again.

tasks.approach: Script.timed wraps a source in `with timeout of N seconds` … `end timeout`, with N = 2 for state, position, modes, track id and artwork and N = 5 for transport commands. Command scripts embed their argument and are not cached, so they are wrapped at build time. A timed-out event returns -1712, which interpret() already maps to .unknown (:395-400), and every other caller already treats a nil descriptor as 'no answer'. The Music artwork script gains the running guard its siblings have. Rejected: a second queue or concurrent NSAppleScript instances, which the code documents as not thread-safe (:440-447); a Swift-side watchdog that abandons the run, which cannot cancel executeAndReturnError and would leave the queue blocked anyway.

(5) testAQuickDoubleTapEndsWhereTheLastTapPointed: the stub records request order and delays the first PUT by 200 ms. After two taps the requests are PUT then DELETE, sequential, and saved[id] is false. Today they run concurrently. (6) testADisconnectDuringALookupLeavesNothingBehind: delay /contains, call disconnect() mid-flight, and assert saved is empty afterwards.
tasks.approach: tokenRequest decodes Spotify's OAuth error body: a 400 with error == invalid_grant becomes .invalidGrant and anything else that is not 200 becomes .failed. On .invalidGrant, freshAccessToken bumps credentialGeneration, clears credentials, sets isConnected = false and needsReconnect = true, and clears saved. A 401 from a library call re-enters freshAccessToken(forceRefresh: true) once, ignoring the cached access token, which also covers the wall-clock expiry stamp when the clock is wrong. A second 401 stops there and marks tokenUnavailable. Library calls use `session`. Writes go through a per-track serialiser: a [trackID: desired Bool] map plus one running Task per track, which loops PUT or DELETE until the server's last answer equals the latest desired value (last tap wins). The optimistic saved flag follows the desired value and rolls back to the server truth on failure. After every await, refreshSavedState and the writer check that credentialGeneration is unchanged. handleCallback sets signInOutcome = .cancelled when the callback carries an error, .expired when no verifier is pending (a relaunch mid sign-in), and .failed when the exchange fails. A successful store clears both flags. Rejected: clearing tokens on any refresh failure, because offline would then disconnect the user; proactive token validation on launch, which adds a network call nobody asked for.

tasks.risks: Spotify's token error body shape ({"error":"invalid_grant"}) is standard OAuth and is assumed. Any other 400 maps to .failed and never disconnects, which is the safe direction. The serialiser must not hold the main actor across awaits; it does not, because each Task hops.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 19 (idle 8 Hz pointer sampler and 2 s geometry watchdog)
decisions_made.decision: Keep both as they are. Measure awake-idle cost (MS-25) and record it as the budget. Any change to either timer goes back to the owner with that number.
decisions_made.reasoning: The sampler decides when the window stops being click-through (PointerWatcher.swift:3-10). Slowing it would let a quick click on the island fall through to the app underneath, which is an interaction defect. Event monitors cannot replace it for an accessory app. The watchdog is a recorded repair for an invisible failure, and the display-sleep path already stops it. CEO policy 3 and 7 apply. MS-12 and MS-13 cut more wakeups on open tabs than any change to these timers would.

decisions_made.decision: Keep the heart. Record it in checklist.md (Spotify account and Lock-screen card entries) and disclose it in Settings › Spotify (MS-09).
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 1: connecting the account is already an opt-in that defaults to off, and the heart is the only reason the account exists (it appears nowhere else, per grep). principles: The user decides what leaves the Shelf. Unmounting a disk (F-001), a weekly inbox prune (F-019) and a Finder move (F-020) each delete or orphan a card today with no word. Apple-design 'Agency' and the recorded checklist line 'deleting it there removes the card' together give the rule: a file that is really gone may leave silently; a file that is only out of reach (offline volume, moved, still referenced) never does.

Read the pasteboard only for what a switch asked for, and never spend a copy the system refused. J-001: ClipboardStore.pollNow advances lastChangeCount at :175-176 and reads .islaInternal data and NSURL objects (:181, :185) before any switch is consulted. The macOS 27 SDK (NSPasteboard.h:55-70, 170) defines accessBehavior with .ask and .alwaysDeny, and says that a programmatic read is what raises the alert.

A cover covers every column that shows the secret, and it never blinds the person typing. F-002: the translation renders with no privacy check (TranslatePane.swift:158-184). F-021: covered = hides && !input.isEmpty hides the editor on its first keystroke (:26-27, :92). Typed text is uncovered on purpose; text that arrives through the hot key stays covered.

Promise only what can be proven. F-008: sharingType = .none is the whole mechanism (NotchPanel.swift:163-168), and whether ScreenCaptureKit honours it on macOS 26 and 27 cannot be settled headlessly. The Settings copy says what the switch asks of macOS and tells the user to use the covers. Live session S7 decides anything stronger.

Off the main thread, applied once. F-022: refreshFromDisk runs checkResourceIsReachable per card on the main actor and asks QuickLook for a new thumbnail for every card on every Shelf open (ShelfStore.swift:180-205). Scan off main, write items once, render each thumbnail once.

Identity by metadata, not by name. G-001: the ScreenCaptureKit lookup returns the key itself. This was re-verified on this Mac: screencaptureui.app's Localizable.loctable has 'Screenshot' = 'Снимок экрана' (ru), 'Bildschirmfoto' (de), 'Знімок екрана' (uk), and both /usr/sbin/screencapture and screencaptureui reference kMDItemIsScreenCapture. J-013: the vault claims every native capture by its prefix (ScreenshotVault.swift:142-149). Both are fixed with the system capture attribute plus an attribute of our own.

Nothing new leaves the Mac without a switch, and no cache holds what did leave. G-016: every third-party request goes through URLSession.shared and its on-disk URLCache (OnlineTranslation.swift:66, OnlineLyrics.swift:119, UpdateCheck.swift:50, SpotifyAccount.swift:133/361/412, PlayerBridge.swift:240). Decision 21: hot-key text goes to MyMemory after 320 ms with no click.

tasks.approach: 1) Add `enum ClipboardAccess { case unknown, ask, allowed, denied }` and `var accessBehavior: () -> ClipboardAccess`. The default maps NSPasteboard.accessBehavior under #available(macOS 15.4, *): .default maps to .unknown, .ask to .ask, .alwaysAllow to .allowed, .alwaysDeny to .denied. Add `@Published private(set) var access`. 2) pollNow: read changeCount. If accessBehavior() == .denied: spend the count, stop(), publish .denied, return. Read `pasteboard.types` once; this is metadata, not content. Return (spending the count) when an opt-out marker or .islaInternal is in types; the marker check moves from data(forType:) to types.contains. 3) A pure `static func readPlan(types:, history:, images:) -> ReadPlan` (files, movieData, image, text, nothing). Files are read only when public.file-url is present and (history || images). An image is read only when images is on and, if history is on, no .string type is present (F-050: text wins). Text is read only when history is on. 4) Spend lastChangeCount only after the planned read returns content, or when the plan is .nothing. If the read returns nil while types promised it: re-ask accessBehavior(). If .denied, enter the denied state. If .allowed, retry the read once now (Allow answered mid-read). Otherwise spend, so the next tick cannot raise a second alert. 5) encodeImage: schedule a retry only while accessBehavior() is .allowed or .unknown and types still list png/tiff. 6) Add the legacy identifiers listed by nspasteboard.org to optOut; check the list against the page at implementation. 7) `func recheckAccess()`: if the state was .denied and access is no longer denied, call startFresh(). CB-02 calls it on Clipboard tab appearance. Rejected: a protocol seam over NSPasteboard. The lazy data provider already counts reads on a real pasteboard, and a protocol would churn every call site. Rejected: polling with detectPatterns. It says nothing about content, so history would have nothing to show. Rejected: stop background reads while access is .unknown. On a Mac that does not enforce the policy, that silently ends history for every current user; it waits for S1.

tasks.title: Copies that arrive while the Mac is locked are not recorded at unlock
tasks.why: G-011: the lock path stops the poll so that Universal Clipboard arrivals are not recorded behind a shield (NotchController.swift:239-247), but start() keeps the old baseline on purpose (ClipboardStore.swift:113-118). The first poll after unlock therefore records what arrived during the lock, against the code's own stated intent.
tasks.failing_test_first: ClipboardStoreTests.testACopyMadeWhileLockedIsNotRecordedAtUnlock: unique pasteboard, store.start(); store.stop(rebaseliningOnResume: true); board.setString('phone copy'); store.start(); store.pollNow(); assert items is empty. Today there is no such parameter; with a plain stop() the item is recorded. Companion testACopyMadeDuringDisplaySleepStillCounts: plain stop(), write, start(), pollNow, one item (holds the existing design).
tasks.approach: ClipboardStore gets a private rebaselineOnStart flag. stop(rebaseliningOnResume: true) sets it; plain stop() leaves it as it is, so a lock followed by display sleep keeps it. start() re-baselines and clears it when set. NotchStores.suspendForIdleScreen gains forLock: Bool = false and passes it through. Both screenLocked() branches (the card-off branch at :205 and :247) pass true. No change to the wake plan: whichever path resumes first re-baselines. Rejected: polling once at lock to catch the copy made just before it. That is a content read at lock time for a window of at most 0.5 s.
tasks.acceptance: Both tests pass. LockedClockTests and NotchController wake-plan tests unchanged. Live S10: an iPhone copy made during a lock is absent from Clipboard after unlock.
tasks.risks: A copy made less than 0.5 s before locking is not recorded. That is acceptable and documented in the comment.

tasks.title: The screenshot vault trims and clears only files it wrote, creates its folder only when it first saves, and survives a deleted folder and same-second saves
tasks.why: J-013: isOwnFile claims any 'Screenshot*.png' or 'Screen Recording*' movie (ScreenshotVault.swift:142-149), which are macOS's own names. The trim past 200 and 'Delete These Files' therefore trash the user's native captures if they live in ~/Pictures/Isla, against the class doc's promise. ~/Pictures/Isla is created at every launch even with the feature off (:18-44). G-022: the folder is never recreated after a user deletes it, and same-second saves race on the concurrent queue (:115-136).

Sources/IslaKit/Model/NotchStores.swift (doc comment that says the vault creates its folder)
tasks.failing_test_first: ScreenshotVaultTests.testANativeCaptureInTheFolderIsNeverClaimed: temp AppPaths; create the pictures dir; write 'Screenshot 2026-10-11 at 15.04.05.png' with the com.apple.metadata:kMDItemIsScreenCapture attribute; assert vault.usage().files == 0 (today 1). Also testInitCreatesNoFolder (today it creates one). Also testAWriteRecreatesADeletedFolder. Also testTwoConcurrentSavesInOneSecondKeepBothFiles (two saves with the same date, not awaited in turn; two distinct files). Also testClearRemovesOnlyMarkedFiles, with a discard seam so the test never moves files into the owner's Trash.
tasks.approach: 1) After a successful write, setxattr com.ctimothe.isla.vault = '1' on the file. 2) isOwnFile: marked, or legacy (name prefix and no kMDItemIsScreenCapture attribute, via CaptureMetadata from SH-03). Files the vault wrote before this change have no system attribute, so they stay manageable; a native capture always has one. 3) init stores paths only. A private serial DispatchQueue (label com.ctimothe.isla.vault, .utility) runs write, trim and clear. Each write resolves the folder (Pictures, else the support fallback, cached after the first success to keep the no-split rule) and runs createDirectory before writing. The collision loop is now race-free because it runs on one queue. 4) usage() and clear() return 0 or do nothing when the folder does not exist. reveal() creates it first, because the user asked to see it. 5) The text fallback for a failed save is not added: after CB-01 a copy that carries text takes the text path, so a failed image save never has text to fall back to. Rejected: a manifest file in the folder. It is extra state that can drift and is visible to the user.
tasks.acceptance: The five tests pass. Existing vault tests pass. NotchStores built in SettingsPaneTests no longer creates ~/Pictures/Isla on the test machine. Live S13 step 5: a copied native capture survives 'Clear Screenshots Folder'.
tasks.risks: Extended attributes do not survive copying the vault to a FAT disk and back; such files fall under the legacy rule. The F-034 race (Delete These Files reloads before the trash runs, feedback group) also edits clear(). Coordinate: if that group adds a completion, keep it on the serial queue.

tasks.title: Dragging a card out copies by default (⌘ moves), the card follows a moved file, and the drag lifts the real thumbnail from where it was grabbed
tasks.why: F-020: the source mask offers .move outside the app (ShelfDragSource.swift:92), so a same-volume Finder drop moves the user's file, and endedAt ignores the result (:95-102), leaving a dead card. F-038: the drag image is a generic 48 pt file icon pinned to the card's corner (:60-68) and mouseDown gives no feedback (:42-45). Apple-design: 'respect the offset from where they grabbed it' and 'respond on pointer-down'.
files: Sources/IslaKit/UI/ShelfDragSource.swift (operationMask, endedAt, dragFrame, mouseDown/mouseUp press callback, image closure)
Sources/IslaKit/UI/ShelfPane.swift (pass item.icon and onPress; press scale)
tasks.failing_test_first: ShelfStoreTests.testAMovedFileKeepsItsCard: temp file A, add([A]) (bookmark made by the default makeBookmark), FileManager.moveItem to B in another temp dir, store.followMove([A]); assert items[0].url == B (resolved) and items.count == 1. Fails today: no followMove. Also ShelfDropTests.testDragOutCopiesUnlessCommandIsHeld: ShelfDragSource.DragView.operationMask(context: .outsideApplication, modifiers: []) == [.copy, .link], and with [.command] it contains .move. Also testDragFrameSitsOverTheThumbnail: dragFrame(index: 0, bounds: 86x92) equals the thumbnail rect (x 9, y 44, 68x40 in unflipped coordinates), and index 1 is offset by the fan step.
tasks.approach: 1) A pure static operationMask, read from NSEvent.modifierFlags in sourceOperationMaskFor; AppKit asks again when modifiers change during a drag. 2) endedAt: if operation contains .move or .delete (drag to Trash), call onMoved(urls), and the card calls shelf.followMove(urls). followMove re-resolves each URL's stored bookmark: a new path updates the card's url in place (keeping its id and selection) and persists; anything unresolvable or in the Trash removes the card. 3) Drag image: urls closure becomes [(URL, NSImage)], with the image taken from the card's cached icon and never a new QuickLook request. The frame is the thumbnail's rect in the card, so a grab inside the thumbnail stays at the same point of the image, with the existing 9 pt fan for a group. 4) Press: mouseDown calls onPress(true); mouseUp and drag end call onPress(false). The card scales to Theme.pressScale (0.97) with Theme.contentAnimation; under Reduce Motion it dims to 0.85 opacity instead. Rejected: removing .move altogether. Finder's ⌘ convention is the expected way to move, and an explicit move then has a card that follows. Rejected: the multi-item count badge from M-21 (no evidence of need; keep the fan).
tasks.acceptance: The three tests pass. Live S13 step 2: dragging a Desktop card to a Finder folder copies it; ⌘-dragging moves it and the card's double-click opens the moved file. Filmed drag: the thumbnail stays under the pointer.
tasks.risks: Changes recorded behaviour ('dragging it out drags the original'): it still drags the original as the source, but the default operation becomes copy, so a same-volume drag now duplicates. Decision 17 is resolved on that basis and is reversible. A dragging source is not retained by AppKit (comment at :113-118), so followMove must be called from endedAt before the view can be torn down; the expiry fail-safe stays.

principles: One persistent, labelled island control. Today the only element that opens Isla is hidden whenever nothing plays (NotchContentView.swift:575 .accessibilityHidden(!shown)); the idle, locked-idle and synthetic-idle lab dumps contain only the bare 700x84 hosting view. A VoiceOver user must always find exactly one 'Isla' button at the notch, whose value says what it shows and whose press opens or closes the panel.

Every pointer-only affordance gets a named accessibility action, never a second hidden path: hover xmarks (ClipboardPane.swift:77-94, ShelfPane.swift:197-211), long press (LyricsStage.swift:476), context menus (ShelfPane.swift:213-221), and the NSView click/drag overlay (ShelfDragSource.swift:32-103). The panel-clipboard dump shows six rows all called 'Copy Entry' and the Shelf dump shows zero card elements, so this is where VoiceOver users are fully blocked.

Every fix is proven headlessly through the accessibility tree. The visual lab already reads SwiftUI's tree offscreen with no window server (VisualLabSupport.swift:321-325 raises AXEnhancedUserInterface, :861-897 walks role, label, value, actions and frame). AX-00 lifts that into an ungated test helper, so each task's failing test is an assertion on role, label, value, actions or frame, and runs in ./scripts/check.

A keyboard open takes the keyboard. A pointer open never does. Panels opened with ⌃⌥⌘I, Show Isla or the island's accessibility action become key, so Escape, Tab and VoiceOver work. The lyrics page opened with ⌃⌥⌘L stays non-key, so a person reading lyrics keeps typing in their own app. Clicks and hovers keep the owner's never-key panel (NotchPanel.swift:5-12).

One feedback surface per event (project non-negotiable 4). Announcements repeat the visible feedback and are never a separate toast. F-013 found no NSAccessibility.post anywhere in Sources. One rate-limited Announcer serves every surface.

A minimum hit target of 24x20 pt, from a Theme token rather than literals. Dump frames today: Clear 27x13, Deselect 44x13, swap 18x14, language chevron 7x4, scrub strip 268x14. Where growing the frame would move a tuned layout (MediaPaneLayoutTests, the WelcomePane fit test), the drawn element keeps its size and the hit region grows.

Honest copy that names the cause and offers only remedies that can work: Launch at Login approval (F-027), quota and guardrail failures (F-042), and AirDrop refusals (F-049). Nothing new leaves the Mac, and nothing changes a system setting without a click.

Recorded owner decisions are kept: click to open, no status item, hover tab switching withdrawn, removed features, and the 0.4 s paused fold (untouched by this group). Where a finding pushes against one, the plan narrows the fix until it fits. Example: 'arriving lands on Music' is kept for the closed island, and only the flip of an already open panel is removed (J-008).

tasks.title: Editing keys follow the layout and Caps Lock; ⇧⌘C copies the translation
tasks.why: ⌘Z on QWERTZ and ⌘A on AZERTY hit the wrong key, because the panel matches US key codes (NotchPanel.swift:45-52). With Caps Lock latched, ⌘A, ⌘X, ⌘C, ⌘V and ⌘Z do nothing, because .capsLock fails the exact-flags test (:104-105). After ⌃⌥⌘T, no key copies the translation: ⌘C and ⌘⇧C both copy the source (:105, :109).
tasks.failing_test_first: PanelKeyRoutingTests: (1) QWERTZ ⌘Z: keyCode 16, characters "z" → .undo; keyCode 6, characters "y" → nil. (2) AZERTY ⌘A: keyCode 12, characters "a" → .selectAll. (3) Russian ⌘C: keyCode 8, characters "с" (U+0441) → .copy, via the key-code fallback. (4) Caps Lock: flags [.command, .capsLock], keyCode 9, characters "v" → .paste. (5) Dvorak-QWERTY⌘: characters "c", charactersIgnoringModifiers "j" → .copy. (6) ⌘⇧C → .copyTranslation. (7) ⌘⌥C → nil. Also build real NSEvent.keyEvent(...) values and route them through the static function.
tasks.approach: flags = modifierFlags ∩ [.command, .control, .option, .shift]; require command and nothing but shift. Letter = the first ASCII letter of `characters` lowercased (this honours Dvorak-QWERTY⌘, where ⌘ switches the layout), else of charactersIgnoringModifiers, else the existing key-code table, which keeps Cyrillic and other non-Latin layouts working (the file's own comment, :40-44). ⇧⌘C returns .copyTranslation. sendEvent calls onCopyTranslation; when that returns false (not on Translate, or no output), it falls back to copy:. vm.copyTranslationIfShowing() copies translator.output and announces 'Copied'. The CopyButton help shows the key. Rejected: ⌘Return for copy (it reads as 'submit/translate' in translators), and installing a main menu (the file explains why an accessory app avoids one, :54-58).
tasks.acceptance: The routing tests pass. Before → after: QWERTZ ⌘Z undo fails → works; Caps Lock paste fails → works; ⇧⌘C copies the source → copies the translation (with a 'Copied' announcement). Live (owner): German layout ⌘Z in Translate; Caps Lock ⌘V.
tasks.risks: Edge layouts where `characters` with ⌘ returns a non-letter fall back to key codes, the same as today, so there is no regression.

tasks.title: A known update survives a later failed or in-flight check, and a rate limit is named
tasks.why: check() sets .checking first and assigns the outcome unconditionally (UpdateCheck.swift:59-78), so a Tuesday offline failure erases Monday's 'Update available'. The rail dot and the Download row vanish. Any non-200, including a 403 rate limit, reads 'Could not reach GitHub'.
tasks.failing_test_first: UpdateCheckTests.testAKnownUpdateSurvivesAFailedRecheck: the fetch stub returns 200 with v9.9.9, then throws URLError(.notConnectedToInternet). After the first check hasUpdate == true. During the second check (state .checking) hasUpdate is still true, and after it fails hasUpdate is still true while state == .failed(.offline). testARateLimitIsNamed: 403 with header x-ratelimit-remaining: 0 → .failed(.rateLimited); 429 → .rateLimited; 500 → .failed(.server).
tasks.approach: Keep `@Published private(set) var lastAvailable: (version: String, page: URL)?`, set on .available and cleared only by a newer .upToDate answer. hasUpdate reads lastAvailable. Settings shows the Download row whenever lastAvailable exists, plus a status line for the latest state. Reasons get copy: offline 'Could not reach GitHub. Try again later.' (existing), rate-limited 'GitHub is limiting checks right now. Try again in an hour.', server 'GitHub did not answer properly. Try again later.'. Automatic checks stay off by default, unchanged.
tasks.acceptance: The tests pass. Before → after: a known update after a failed recheck is lost → kept; a rate limit reads as 'could not reach' → named.
tasks.risks: none (no new network calls, and the default is unchanged)
tasks.strings_and_tokens: "GitHub is limiting checks right now. Try again in an hour." = ru "GitHub сейчас ограничивает проверки. Попробуйте через час."; "GitHub did not answer properly. Try again later." = ru "GitHub ответил с ошибкой. Попробуйте позже."

tasks.title: Online translation: capped, keeps what it got, and offers Retry only when Retry can work
tasks.why: Online translation sends unbounded sequential 480-character requests and throws away everything on the first failure (OnlineTranslation.swift:65-84). Every failure offers Retry (Translator.swift:464-465), including a used-up daily quota and Apple's guardrail, which cannot succeed on retry.
files: Sources/IslaKit/Services/Translator.swift (describe → (message, retryable); translate() remedies; online seam onlineTranslate)
tasks.failing_test_first: TranslatorTests.testAQuotaFailureOffersNoRetry: inject onlineTranslate throwing .quotaExhausted, with capabilities that only online can serve; after translate(), remedies == [] and failure == "Today's free online translations are used up.". testAGuardrailOrTooLongOffersNoRetry; testUnreachableOffersRetry. OnlineTranslationTests.testInputBeyondTheCapIsNotSent: a URLProtocol stub counts requests for 10,000 characters; at most 10 requests (4,800 characters). testALaterChunkFailingKeepsEarlierText: chunk 1 OK, chunk 2 quota → Failure.partial(text: chunk1 translation, cause: .quotaExhausted).
tasks.approach: maximumOnlineCharacters = 4,800 (10 chunks). Verify against MyMemory's published anonymous daily allowance before landing; if it differs, the cap follows it. Text beyond the cap is not sent, and the result line says "Only the first 4,800 characters were translated online." A partial result shows the translated part plus the cause, with no Retry when the cause is quota. describe returns retryable: unreachable and generic yes; quotaExhausted, guardrailViolation and exceededContextWindowSize no, with the too-long message gaining 'Shorten it and try again.'. Remedies come from retryable. Rejected: parallel chunk requests (burns the quota faster, and the service throttles).
tasks.acceptance: The tests pass. Before → after: Retry offered on quota or guardrail yes → no; 100 KB online → 209 requests before, ≤ 10 after; partial work after a mid-text failure is discarded → kept.
tasks.risks: The translate group (H-005, G-014, G-026) and the privacy-consent group (M-25 ask-before-online) edit Translator. Sequence after them, or keep this to describe(), remedies and OnlineTranslation.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: "Only the first %@ characters were translated online." = ru "Онлайн переведены только первые %@ символов."; "This text is too long to translate at once. Shorten it and try again." = ru "Этот текст слишком длинный для перевода за раз. Сократите его и попробуйте снова." (replaces the old too-long key)

tasks.title: Re-check a synthetic notch after every rebuild, not only at launch
tasks.why: verifySyntheticNotch runs only from install() (NotchController.swift:130, :379-391). A display rearrangement that reads a zero safe area for a moment leaves a synthetic pill drawn on a notched Mac until some later notification.
tasks.failing_test_first: SyntheticRecheckTests.testASyntheticBuildSchedulesRechecks: NotchController.recheckDelays(isPhysical: false) == [1.5, 5.0] and (isPhysical: true) == []. A spy on a new `scheduleRecheck` seam, called from rebuild(), receives the delays. The test fails because rebuild never schedules them today.
tasks.approach: Extract the delays into a pure static and call verifySyntheticNotch() at the end of rebuild(). The existing guards (re-read isPhysical before rebuilding; nothing happens once physical) prevent loops. Stale work items check the current viewModel's geometry, as they already do.

tasks.why: After the P1 fixes, the largest accessibility gain left (Mobbin M-39) is letting keyboard users work the Clipboard and the Shelf without pointing. It builds on KB-01's key panel and on CB-01 and SF-01's per-row elements.

On Shelf: right → next card, Space → .quickLook, Return → .open. On Translate → nil, because the text view owns the keys.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 1 (keyboard navigation inside the panel)
decisions_made.decision: Adopt in three steps, without changing the pointer model. KB-01: keyboard-opened panels (⌃⌥⌘I, Show Isla, the AX action, the welcome) become key, while click and hover opens stay never-key and ⌃⌥⌘L stays non-key so typing continues. KB-06: ⌘1–⌘5 and Tab focus with the system ring. KB-07: list keys. Type-to-filter is deferred.
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 2: accessibility beats taste. Full Keyboard Access users are blocked from four of five tabs today. Limiting key status to keyboard opens keeps the owner's reason for a never-key panel ('too rude for a panel one merely hovers', NotchPanel.swift:5-12) intact for pointer users.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 2 (Settings toggles with a detached label)
decisions_made.decision: The whole row is the toggle's hit target, with a drawn on-state that does not depend on key status (SET-01).
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 2. Native labelled toggles toggle on their label. The mini switch is 36x16 and draws as inactive (H-002, four personas).

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 3 (Escape and two-press confirmations; 3 s disarm)
decisions_made.decision: Escape disarms an armed confirmation before it closes anything. Arming is announced. The disarm timer pauses while hovered and runs 8 s instead of 3 s while VoiceOver is on (AN-02).
decisions_made.reasoning: On macOS Escape means cancel, so the nearest cancellable thing goes first, consistent with consumeEscape's own design. VoiceOver users need time to reach the control again.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 4 (hand-rolled choiceRow segmented control)
decisions_made.decision: Keep the drawn capsules, and expose a native segmented Picker through accessibilityRepresentation (SET-02). The 'Glass title equals its first option' half is stale: the options now read Transparent, Tinted and Solid.
decisions_made.reasoning: This gives radio-group semantics without the AppKit look the owner objected to on a dark pane. Policy 2 is met without overriding the visual choice.

decisions_made.decision: No Isla toggle. Record in checklist.md (with SET-08) that the two haptic moments follow the system's trackpad haptic setting, and verify that live.
decisions_made.reasoning: There are only two sparing moments (checklist.md:172-175). A per-app switch adds a row for no measured need, and the system setting is the user's existing control. If the live check shows NSHapticFeedbackManager ignores the system setting, add the switch.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 8 (Reduce Motion removes the locked-island refusal)
decisions_made.decision: The refusal is now announced to VoiceOver on every route (AN-01, SH-01). A non-travel visual channel for sighted Reduce Motion users is left to the motion-reduce group, alongside F-018 and H-022.
decisions_made.reasoning: One feedback surface per event: the announcement mirrors the refusal and is not a second toast. The visual redesign of the shake belongs to the group fixing whether it plays at all.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 15 (Escape in Translate clears typed text)
decisions_made.decision: Keep the behaviour, and correct the doc comment that calls it reversible (AN-02).
decisions_made.reasoning: First Escape clears, second closes: this matches NSSearchField and Spotlight, so it is native. The only defect is the false 'reversible' claim.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Wave A decision 24 (arrow cursor pinned over the Translate editor)
decisions_made.decision: Show an I-beam over the editor and the arrow elsewhere (PTR-02).
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 2: native beats taste. Every text field on macOS shows an I-beam.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: J-008 ('arriving always lands on Music', OpenOnClickTests:100)
decisions_made.decision: Keep 'arriving lands on Music' for the closed island. An arrival on an already open panel only drops the pin (KB-03), recorded as a dated amendment under the 2026-09-10 pin amendment.
decisions_made.reasoning: CEO policy 3. The recorded rationale (the island is for glancing at a track; other tabs are somewhere to go once open) is about arriving at the island, not about using an open panel. The existing test keeps passing unchanged.

decisions_made.owner_decision_ref: Mobbin M-39 (needs owner decision: list keyboard model)
decisions_made.decision: Adopted as KB-07, without type-to-filter, only for key (keyboard-opened) panels.
decisions_made.reasoning: Under CEO policy 2 the accessibility gain wins, and limiting it to keyboard opens avoids changing the never-key contract for pointer users. The filter is new feature scope.

deferred.item: Volume or brightness HUD replacement
deferred.reason: Owner-level product decision (CEO policy 4). Trade-off: a native-feeling HUD at the notch is a strong differentiator, but it needs a system-key event tap (Accessibility permission) or private APIs, it changes a system behaviour, and Mobbin holds no reference screens.

deferred.item: Developer ID signing and an in-app updater (Sparkle)
deferred.reason: Owner-level (CEO policy 4). Trade-off: Gatekeeper's malware alert on the helper dylib (memory) and manual updates hurt every stranger, but both need the paid Apple Developer membership and a release-owner key. SET-06 only fixes the existing check.

deferred.item: Owner decision 5: collapseRectShrinkDelay 0.45 s swallows clicks on the retracting body
deferred.reason: Depends on the motion group's close choreography (H-012, H-013), which changes the close curve. Retune it after that lands, deriving the delay from the spring's settle time instead of a literal.

deferred.item: Owner decision 6: Panel Width live preview
deferred.reason: Not an accessibility defect. A live preview would rebuild the panel per tick (audit A7: about 140 teardowns per drag). Recommend the ghost-outline idea from Mobbin's below-the-cut list as a later visual task, after PTR-01 makes the drag reliable.

deferred.item: Owner decision 10: Dynamic Type or a larger-text option
deferred.reason: Accessibility favours it, but the panel is a fixed 700x444 window with a 208 pt body and measured fits (the WelcomePane fit test, MediaPaneLayoutTests). A one-step Larger Text needs a layout pass over every pane. Recommend the owner choose between recording the divergence in checklist.md now and scheduling a dedicated L-sized larger-text project.

deferred.item: Owner decision 16: pointer-away folds the panel while typing in Translate
deferred.reason: This is the documented 'the pointer decides' rule (NotchController.swift:1135-1152), and the Accessibility Keyboard and head-pointer users are the casualties. Recommended fix for the owner: treat 'the field holds the keyboard' like a pin (ends on Escape, click outside, ⌘-Tab or the hot key), which pairs naturally with KB-01. It reverses a stated rule, so it needs the owner's yes.

deferred.item: H-011 visual half (an interlude glyph or progress fill on the empty current row)

principles: Contrast is computed against the brightest backdrop a surface can actually have, not against black. ContrastRampTests only measures over black today, which is how the lock card shipped at 1.76:1 (cardSecondary) and 1.59:1 (cardTertiary) over a white cover (LockScreenCard.swift:220, wash 0.34 gives a 168-grey backdrop). Every new contrast test composites the token over the worst permitted fill or cover.

Accessibility beats taste, and native beats invented (CEO policy 2). Evidence: tertiary 0.46 is 4.29:1 on Theme.surface and 3.52:1 on surfaceHover; lyric context lines 0.28/0.34 are 2.27:1/2.89:1; the output picker's white glyph on a yellow controlAccentColor is about 1.4:1; Settings switches draw in AppKit's inactive style because the panel is never key (lab finding 9).

Exits start fast and run on the path the entrance used (apple-design skill, section 'Enter and exit along the same path'). paneOut is an ease-in 0.12 s that starts at 0/s, so the body is still 0.93 opaque when the clip has travelled the 14 pt bottom padding (model: open spring 0.34 s over 176 pt). The open was fixed for this with a 40 ms delayed paneIn; the close never was.

Reduce Motion means a gentler equivalent with no vestibular jump, not nothing (apple-design section 14). Today the Reduce Motion open is an ease-out 0.12 s that moves 38.6 pt in its first frame and peaks at 2,518 pt/s, about twice the spring it replaces (1,197 pt/s). The refusal shake disappears entirely under Reduce Motion.

An explicit, dated owner request is never reversed (CEO policy 3). The fold stays above 0.4 s because on 2026-09-21 the owner called the 0.28 s fold a snap ('too intense, too raw'). The hover-nudge bump stays because the owner asked for it on 2026-09-21. The 0.4 s paused fold and click-to-open are not touched.

A binding record beats an unsettled code path. checklist.md says the lock card's glass is a drawn recipe because nothing above the shield can be sampled. The code still hands a no-cover card, and its output popover, to glassEffect on macOS 26 (LockScreenCard.swift:155, :527).

Measure language and layout instead of counting characters. A single 'ү' makes a whole Russian paragraph Kazakh, and with Translate Online on it goes to MyMemory (TranslationLanguage.swift:127). The type ladder sizes by total character count, so 'железнодорожная' breaks mid-word at 27 pt in a 219 pt column (TranslatePane.swift:225-236).

Copy follows Apple's own Russian tables when there is a question. AppKit's Ruler.loctable maps 'pt' to 'пт', so 'пт' stays. Control Center's Sound.loctable maps 'Output' to 'Выход' and 'Output device' to 'Устройство выхода звука', so 'Вывод' goes.

Every value change is held by a closed-form test (the PillFoldTests style: critically damped springs as (1+ωt)e^(−ωt), SwiftUI's ease curves as their cubic Béziers) before any visual-lab render is read. Keyframes are reconstructions, so feel is a live check.

tasks.title: The lock card stays readable over a pale cover: a wash scaled to the cover's brightness and brighter card tokens
tasks.why: Persona-confirmed P1. Over a near-white cover in the default Tinted style the artist line (cardSecondary 0.62) measures 1.76:1, the elapsed time and status (cardTertiary 0.50) 1.59:1, and pure white 2.37:1 (computed: wash 0.34 over sRGB 1.0 gives 0.66 grey). Render: lock-card/clear-standard-lyrics__light-ir.png. Dark covers already read well and must not get darker.
tasks.failing_test_first: ContrastRampTests.testEveryCardLabelHoldsAAOverTheBrightestCover: for increaseContrast in [false, true], let bg = LockCardLegibility.backdrop(coverLuma: 1.0, style: .glass, increaseContrast:); assert contrast(cardSecondaryOpacity, bg) >= 4.5 and contrast(cardTertiaryOpacity, bg) >= 4.5. It fails today: the helper does not exist, and the current constants give 1.76 and 1.59. Alongside it: testADarkCoverKeepsTheLightItHad asserts washOpacity(coverLuma: 0.25, style: .glass, increaseContrast: false) == 0.34, so a dark cover keeps today's look. And LockCardCoverLightTests.testCoverLumaReadsWhiteAsOneAndBlackAsZero uses generated 64×64 NSImages, plus a half-white image that reads at least 0.9 at the 90th percentile.
tasks.approach: 1) Pure LockCardLegibility. contrast() is WCAG over a grey composite (gamma-space source-over, which matches how SwiftUI composites these layers). washOpacity solves by bisection for the smallest α ≥ floor (0.34 normal, 0.56 Increase Contrast, today's values) at which cardTertiary over coverLuma·(1−α) is at least 4.5:1. 2) coverLuma(of:) draws the NSImage into an 8×8 sRGB CGContext with high interpolation, takes the 90th percentile of relative luminance, and re-encodes it to sRGB. It is cached in an NSCache keyed by ObjectIdentifier(image), so it runs once per artwork, which changes once per track. 3) coverLight uses Color.black.opacity(washOpacity(...)) in place of the fixed 0.34/0.2/0.56 and keeps the bottom gradient. 4) Card tokens are rounded up, never down, keeping the file's existing rule: cardSecondary 0.62→0.75 and cardTertiary 0.50→0.62 (Increase Contrast stays 0.85/0.75, still higher). testTheCardRunsBrighterThanThePanel still holds. 5) Transparent (.clear): the wash is applied to the cover part. The 38% of wallpaper that shows through cannot be known above the shield, so checklist.md records it as a deliberate divergence: Tinted and Solid guarantee 4.5:1 and Increase Contrast already makes Transparent opaque. Rejected: a fixed 0.70 wash, which darkens every dark cover and undoes the owner's 2026-09-21 'lit by its own cover'. Rejected: a light-card flip (M-5 already rejected it for the flash on track change). Rejected: text colour chosen per pixel, which is not native.
tasks.acceptance: Unit: over a white cover in Tinted, cardSecondary goes from 1.76:1 to 5.7:1 (0.75 at α≈0.705) and cardTertiary from 1.59:1 to at least 4.5:1, and the same at Increase Contrast. Covers with 90th-percentile luma ≤ 0.3 keep α = 0.34. Visual lab: re-run `bash Scripts/visual-lab.sh <out> VisualLabIslandTests` and compare lock-card/clear-standard-lyrics__light-ir.png and glass-standard-player__dark-ir.png before and after. Optionally, add a lab metric that samples backdrop luminance in the -ir render at the artist row and the time labels and prints the ratio into metrics.json. ./scripts/check green.
tasks.risks: The 8×8 draw decodes the artwork once per track on the main actor. It is cheap next to the 44 pt live blur that already decodes it (F-044, perf group, may move decoding off main; coverLuma should then read their thumbnail). Raising card tokens brightens the volume glyphs and the picker header slightly. Saturation 1.3 on the blurred cover is ignored by the luma model (it changes chroma more than luminance); the render pass confirms.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: No strings. Tokens: cardSecondaryOpacity 0.62→0.75, cardTertiaryOpacity 0.50→0.62. The wash comes from LockCardLegibility, not a literal.

tasks.title: One foreign character no longer decides the language of a whole text
tasks.why: A Russian paragraph quoting 'Нұрсұлтан' is labelled 'Kazakh (Detected)', and with Translate Online on the whole paragraph goes to MyMemory. That sends text off the Mac on a misdetection. tasks.failing_test_first: LanguageDetectionTests.testOneForeignLetterDoesNotDecideAParagraph: a Russian paragraph of about 250 letters containing 'Нұрсұлтан' detects as .russian (today .kazakh). 'I had 寿司 for lunch with my friends today' detects as .english (today .japanese). Must stay green: 'Сіз қалайсыз?' → .kazakh, 'Қаерга борасиз?' → .uzbek, 'こんにちは' → .japanese, and every existing case in testAScriptOfItsOwnDecidesEvenOneWord. TranslatorTests: Translator.route(for: thatParagraph, source: nil, target: .english).source == .russian.
tasks.approach: Count letters (Character.isLetter) once. byLetters decides Kazakh or Uzbek only when its distinctive letters are at least 2% of the Cyrillic letters. Real Kazakh and Uzbek run at 5-8%, and a short Kazakh word ('Сәлем') is 20%. byScript decides a script only when its letters are at least 30% of all letters. Kana or Han together at 30% or more counts as CJK, and any kana inside CJK means Japanese. Anything mixed falls through to NLLanguageRecognizer, which is constrained to the offered languages as today. Rejected: running the recognizer first, which misreads Uzbek (measured 2026-09-21, documented in the file).
tasks.acceptance: All LanguageDetectionTests green, including the new cases. The misdetected Russian paragraph is no longer routed online.
tasks.risks: Very short mixed strings ('OK 寿司') now reach the recognizer. Its short-text confidence rule then falls back to the Cyrillic/English rule, which is the documented behaviour.

tasks.title: The locked island's refusal plays on every click, keeps its beat, and has a Reduce Motion form
tasks.why: The shake almost certainly never plays. The locked branch's `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` (NotchContentView.swift:139-140) wipes RefusalShake's withAnimation (RefusalShake.swift:33). From a resting progress of 1, writing 0 then animating to 1 in one pass nets no change, so a second click cannot replay it. If it did play, the sine runs on ease-out progress: an 8.8 pt jump in the first frame and a beat that halves (animation/refusal-shake-offset.csv). Under Reduce Motion the refusal is removed entirely (owner decision 8).
files: Tests/IslaKitTests/VisualLabAnimationTests.swift (sample RefusalShake.offset(at:) instead of parsing the withAnimation literal at :180 and :387-395)
tasks.failing_test_first: RefusalShakeTests.testTheShakeStartsGentlyAndKeepsItsBeat: RefusalShake.offset(at: 0) == 0; abs(offset(at: 1.0/60)) ≤ 3; the zero crossings sit at k·duration/(2·shakes) ± 2 ms (equal spacing); offset(at: duration) == 0; max |offset| ≤ standardAmplitude. testReduceMotionDipsInsteadOfMoving: reducedOpacity(at: 0) == 1, reducedOpacity(at: duration/2) ≤ 0.5, reducedOpacity(at: duration) == 1. Fails today: neither static exists.
tasks.approach: Time-driven rather than transaction-driven. @State startedAt: Date? is set to .now on every trigger change. TimelineView(.animation(paused: startedAt == nil)) draws content.offset(x: offset(at: elapsed)), or under Reduce Motion content.opacity(reducedOpacity(at: elapsed)). A .task(id: trigger) clears startedAt after the duration. Every click restarts from zero, and because no Animation is involved, the locked branch's nil transaction (which keeps the lock a cut) cannot cancel it. offset(at:) = A · min(1, t/0.04) · (1 − t/T) · sin(2π·shakes·t/T): a linear phase with a decaying envelope ramped in over 40 ms, T = 0.5, shakes = 3, A = 11. The Reduce Motion dip goes 1 → 0.45 → 1 over 0.36 s on the pill content only. The black shape stays, so nothing shows through the cutout. Rejected: keyframeAnimator (whether a disabled transaction suppresses it cannot be proven offscreen). Rejected: removing the locked branch's nil transaction (load-bearing: it stops the card and the pill sliding in from the old frame).
tasks.acceptance: Unit tests green. Visual lab animation/refusal-shake-offset.csv: first frame 8.8 pt → ≤ 3 pt (2.6 pt modelled); half-periods equal at 83 ms, where today they stretch over the shake.
